Priya Nair: quick sync—following the RFC, we need a compact manifest format for quant profiles that enables fast runtime aliasing + safe hotpatches. aim: tiny, versioned, O(1) lookup.

Jonah Kim: agree. constraints: <1KB per model manifest, single lookup per request, backwards compat with X-Quant-Profile header.

Lena Ortiz: proposal: manifest rows are CSV-like lines, e.g.:

```
alias_id,primary_profile,fallbacks,quality_tag,flags,version
fp8-lite~v1,fp8-lite,int8-fallback|int4-fallback,medium,kv_ok;attn_ok,2026-03-15-1
```

Lena Ortiz: runtime loads manifest into a hashmap keyed by alias_id and primary_profile. fallback list is pipe-separated. flags are bitflags for runtime capabilities.

Marcus Hall: hotpatching: control-plane publishes new manifest version; runtime responds with ACK. if ack missing for 2m, control-plane retries. hotfixes use a `hotfix` suffix in version and require manual approval.

Jonah Kim: telemetry: emit `quant.manifest.version_applied` gauge and `quant.fallbacks.count` counter. alert if unexpected fallback rate > 1% for 6h for customers > baseline.

Priya Nair: compatibility: for 45 days include both headers `X-Quant-Profile` and `X-Quant-Alias`. after that, drop legacy header. SDKs should tolerate `quant_resolution` optional body: `{alias,applied}` if client asks with `X-Quant-Explain:1`.

Lena Ortiz: runtime impl note: keep manifest parsing lock-free—use copy-on-write pointer swap. allow up to 5m staleness. preserve monotonic version string to detect out-of-order publishes.

Marcus Hall: ops runbook: 1) publish manifest to canary (1%), watch `fallbacks.count`, latency; 2) 10% for 4h; 3) full rollout. rollback: republish previous version and force ack cycle.

Priya Nair: owner assignments: Jonah -> manifest API + schema, Lena -> runtime loader + shim, Marcus -> rollout playbook, Priya -> SDK compatibility notes. I'll open the initial PRs.
